title: The Crab That Split in Fives
story: In the black-glass caves under a sleeping volcano, Mr 6 meets Ashgorrow, a crab of hot cinders who splits into five smaller crabs every single time a sword taps its shell. Three cave-miners are trapped behind the skittering swarm. Mr 6 lowers his sword and starts counting instead.
question: There is 1 crab now. If Mr 6 struck it, and then struck every crab that appeared, and did that for 3 rounds in a row, how many crabs would be scuttling around at the end?
solution: Round 2: 5 x 5 = 25 crabs. Round 3: 25 x 5 = 125 crabs.
So striking three rounds would make 125 crabs — which is exactly why Mr 6 does not strike.
praise: Multiplying by 5 was precisely the right move — the swarm just needed one more round of multiplying, not adding.
hint: Each round multiplies the whole swarm by 5, not just the original crab. Try writing 1, then 5, then...
victory: Mr 6 sheathes his sword, tips a bucket of cool spring water on the cinder crab, and Ashgorrow shrinks to the size of a teacup and clicks its claws politely. The miners walk out laughing.
imagePrompt: A glowing ember-shelled crab in a volcanic obsidian cave, faint copies of itself flickering into being, as a numeral-six knight thoughtfully sheathes his sword by the light of a spring-water bucket.
